title: Santa Claus tradition traced back to the Sami
place_text: New York, Netherlands, Germany, Italy, Turkey, Lapland

tellings.quote: If you follow the routes like how it came to the US to New York through the Dutch, the Dutch had Sinterklaas, their own version of Santa Claus.

plain: The Santa Claus tradition can be followed back along its routes to the Sami, the reindeer-herding people of Lapland in the far north of Europe. Tero Isokauppila, a Finnish entrepreneur who works with mushrooms, tells Michels it came to New York through the Dutch, who had "Sinterklaas, their own version of Santa Claus," and traces it back through Germany, Italy and Turkey, without naming a source. If he is right, a modern Christmas figure would carry traces of an old northern tradition.
